paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: gifts are for building people up, not for putting on a show. Paul tells the Corinthians to "strive to excel in gifts that build up the church" (1 Corinthians 14:12). He's not tossing tongues out of the kitchen, because he says he wishes all of them could speak in tongues (1 Corinthians 14:5). He just wants whatever you bring to the table to feed somebody besides you.

So what does that look like for a baker today? Paul says he would rather speak "five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue" (1 Corinthians 14:19). Love comes first, and then clear words, spoken so the person next to you can actually understand them and say "Amen" with you (1 Corinthians 14:1, 16). Paul also says he will pray and sing with his spirit and with his mind (1 Corinthians 14:15), so he keeps both going. That's the whole recipe, friend, and nobody has to guess what's in it.

Here's why it matters: Paul tells them to eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially prophecy, because the one who prophesies edifies the church (1 Corinthians 14:1, 4). When everyone is prophesying and an unbeliever walks in, he will be convicted, the secrets of his heart will be made known, and he will fall facedown and worship, proclaiming, "God is truly among you!" (1 Corinthians 14:24-25). THAT is the goal, friend, and it's a lot bigger than any of us getting the spotlight. So this week, ask who your words will build up, and keep your apron on, because Paul isn't done teaching this church yet.
